paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university sports facilities should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您的大学正在征求学生关于大学体育设施是否应向公众开放的意见。你现在要写一篇文章来表达你的观点。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Over the coming decades, millions of jobs will be threatened by robotics and artificial intelligence. Despite intensive academic 26 on these developments, there has been little study on how workers 27 to being replaced through technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: 未来几十年，数以百万计的工作岗位将受到机器人和人工智能的威胁。尽管学术界对这些发展进行了激烈的争论，但很少有人研究工人对被技术取代有何反应。

paragraphs.sourceText: To find out, business researchers at TUM and Erasmus University Rotterdam conducted 11 studies and surveys with over 2,000 persons from several countries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了找到答案，慕尼黑工业大学和鹿特丹伊拉斯姆斯大学的商业研究人员对来自多个国家的 2,000 多人进行了 11 项研究和调查。

paragraphs.sourceText: The findings show: In principle, most people view it more 28 when workers are replaced by other people than by robots or intelligent software. This preference 29 , however, when it refers to people’s own jobs. When that is the case, the majority of workers find it less upsetting to see their own jobs go to robots than to other employees. In the long term, however, the same people see machines as more threatening to their future role in the workforce. These effects can also be observed among people who have recently become unemployed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究结果表明：原则上，大多数人对工人被其他人取代而不是被机器人或智能软件取代更有利。然而，当涉及到人们自己的工作时，这种偏好就会逆转。在这种情况下，大多数工人发现自己的工作被机器人取代比其他员工更不那么沮丧。然而，从长远来看，这些人认为机器对他们未来在劳动力中的角色构成更大的威胁。这些影响也可以在最近失业的人中观察到。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers were able to identify the causes behind these 30 paradoxical results, too: People tend to 31 themselves less with machines than with other people. Consequently, being replaced by a robot or software 32 less of a threat to their feeling of self-worth. This reduced self-threat could even be observed when participants assumed that they were being replaced by other employees who relied on technological abilities such as artificial intelligence in their work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员也能够找出这些看似矛盾的结果背后的原因：人们倾向于较少将自己与机器进行比较，而不是与其他人进行比较。因此，被机器人或软件取代对他们的自我价值感的威胁较小。当参与者认为自己正在被其他依赖人工智能等技术能力的员工取代时，这种自我威胁的减少甚至可以被观察到。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Even when unemployment results from the 33 of new technologies, people still judge it in a social context,” says Christoph Fuchs, one of the authors of the study. “It is important to understand these 34 effects when trying to manage the massive changes in the working world to minimize 35 in society.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究的作者之一克里斯托夫·福克斯（Christoph Fuchs）表示：“即使失业是由于新技术的引入造成的，人们仍然会在社会背景下对其进行判断。” “当试图应对工作世界的巨大变化以尽量减少对社会的干扰时，了解这些心理影响非常重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: No escape as “snow day” becomes “e-learning day”
paragraphs.translationZh: “下雪日”变成“电子学习日”，无处可逃

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Certain institutions, such as schools, are likely to close when bad weather, such as snow, flooding or extreme heat or cold, causes travel difficulties, power outages (断供), or otherwise endangers public safety. When snowy weather arrives in the U.S., it means the chance of school children benefiting from the long-standing tradition of the “snow day”, when schools are forced to close and students get an unexpected day off.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 当雪、洪水、极热或极冷等恶劣天气导致出行困难、断电或以其他方式危及公共安全时，某些机构（例如学校）可能会关闭。当美国下雪时，这意味着学童有机会受益于“雪日”的悠久传统，学校被迫停课，学生们可以享受意外的休息日。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The criterion for a snow day is primarily the inability of school buses to operate safely on their routes and danger to children who walk to school. Often, the school remains officially open even though buses do not run and classes are canceled. Severe weather that causes cancellation or delay is more likely in regions that are less able to handle the situation. Snow days are less common in more northern areas of the United States that are used to heavy winter snowfall, because municipalities are well equipped to clear roads and remove snow. In areas less accustomed to snow even small snowfalls of an inch or two may render roads unsafe.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 下雪天的标准主要是校车无法在其路线上安全运行以及对步行上学的儿童造成危险。通常，即使公交车不运行且课程取消，学校仍保持正式开放。在处理能力较弱的地区，因恶劣天气导致航班取消或延误的可能性更大。在习惯了冬季大雪的美国北部地区，下雪天不太常见，因为市政当局拥有完善的设备来清理道路和除雪。在不习惯下雪的地区，即使是一两英寸的小雪也可能导致道路不安全。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Snow days are a familiar theme in American film and TV shows, with children getting the good news and then running outside for some seasonal snowman-building and snowball throwing, against a background of joyful pop music. But the tradition is now over for pupils in several U.S. states such as South Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Indiana. This academic year, many school boards have introduced policies which require students to work from home if the school is shut by snow or extreme weather. They are known as “e-learning days”, which certainly sounds less fun than a snow day.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 下雪天是美国电影和电视节目中常见的主题，孩子们听到好消息后，在欢快的流行音乐背景下跑到外面堆雪人和扔雪球。但对于美国南卡罗来纳州、内华达州、佐治亚州和印第安纳州等几个州的学生来说，这一传统已经结束。本学年，许多学校董事会出台了政策，要求学生在学校因大雪或极端天气而关闭时在家工作。它们被称为“电子学习日”，这听起来肯定没有下雪天那么有趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Teachers are also losing their snow days and instead will be expected to be on hand to take a virtual register and answer students’ questions online. A pilot programme in a school district in Anderson County, South Carolina, has supplied students with electronic tablets loaded with assignments to complete in the event of a school closure. If it is successful, it could be rolled out across the state.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 老师们也不再下雪了，而是需要在现场进行虚拟登记并在线回答学生的问题。南卡罗来纳州安德森县一个学区的一个试点项目为学生提供了电子平板电脑，其中载有学校停课时需要完成的作业。如果成功，可能会在全州推广。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) But some parents object to the new policy if the vigorous debate on the Facebook page of Anderson County school district is anything to go by. “When it snows, let the kids enjoy it,” said one commenter. Another said the decision would “ruin school even more”, and someone else called snow days “a fun part of childhood”. But supporters of the policy say it means children will miss fewer days of school. It will also bring to an end a less popular U.S. high school tradition: the “make-up day”, which requires students in many states to make up the time lost due to weather by working during school holidays.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 但是，如果安德森县学区 Facebook 页面上的激烈辩论是事实的话，一些家长反对这项新政策。 “下雪的时候，让孩子们享受吧，”一位评论者说。另一位人士表示，这一决定将“进一步破坏学校”，还有人称下雪天是“童年的有趣部分”。但该政策的支持者表示，这意味着孩子们缺课的天数将会减少。它还将结束一个不太受欢迎的美国高中传统：“补课日”，该传统要求许多州的学生在学校假期期间通过打工来弥补因天气原因而损失的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Students in North Carolina already have several make-up days scheduled because of school closures during Hurricane Florence, which struck in September. Tom Wilson, the superintendent ( 主管) of Anderson County school district, said the change away from snow days makes practical and financial sense. He said technology has changed every profession, so it makes sense to use it to “eliminate” make-up days. Adam Baker of the Department of Education in Indiana said e-learning days were proving a “great success”. He said most Indiana schools already use digital devices during lessons, so it was an “easy decision” to extend this to days when schools are closed. He denies the decision is depriving children of the chance to enjoy the snow. “Students are still able to enjoy snow days and outside time,” he said. “Many have PE and science assignments that have them out enjoying the weather.” But local school superintendents in Ohio are resisting proposals to adopt e-learning days. They fear that students without internet access at home will be disadvantaged by the policy, and superintendent Tom Roth is concerned that e-learning days will offer a lower quality of education.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 由于 9 月份飓风佛罗伦萨期间学校停课，北卡罗来纳州的学生已经安排了几天补课。安德森县学区主管汤姆·威尔逊 (Tom Wilson) 表示，取消下雪天的做法具有实际意义和经济意义。他说，技术已经改变了每个职业，因此用它来“消除”化妆是有意义的。印第安纳州教育部的亚当·贝克 (Adam Baker) 表示，事实证明，电子学习日取得了“巨大成功”。他说，大多数印第安纳州学校已经在上课时使用数字设备，因此将其延长到学校停课的日子是一个“简单的决定”。他否认这一决定剥夺了孩子们享受雪的机会。 “学生们仍然可以享受下雪天和户外活动，”他说。 “许多人都有体育和科学作业，让他们出去享受天气。”但俄亥俄州当地的学校负责人拒绝采用电子学习日的提议。他们担心在家无法上网的学生会因该政策而处于不利地位，而学监汤姆·罗斯则担心电子学习日会降低教育质量。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) There are also so-called “blizzard bags”, with assignments that children take home ahead of an expected snow closure. But Mr Roth says it is not sufficient as a replacement. “I think we still need the class time to give our kids the education that they deserve,” he said. “You can’t get that with a blizzard bag or doing the work from home like that. It’s not going to be as effective.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 还有所谓的“暴风雪袋”，里面装着孩子们在预计封雪之前带回家的作业。但罗斯先生表示，这不足以作为替代品。 “我认为我们仍然需要上课时间来为我们的孩子提供他们应得的教育，”他说。 “你无法通过防风袋或像这样在家工作来做到这一点。它不会那么有效。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) There is a long-running debate on whether missing days of school affects attainment. In England, there has been a focus on tackling absenteeism (旷课) from school. The Department for Education (DFE) published research in 2016 arguing that missing any days at school could have a negative impact on results. Even a few days lost in a year could be enough to miss out on getting a good exam grade, the DFE’s research concluded. This differed from the findings of a study from Harvard University in the U.S., which concluded that missing a few occasional days because of the weather did not damage learning.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 关于缺课是否影响学业成绩存在长期争论。在英国，解决旷课问题一直是一个重点。教育部 (DFE) 于 2016 年发表研究，认为缺课可能会对成绩产生负面影响。 DFE 的研究得出结论，即使一年中损失了几天的时间，也足以导致无法获得良好的考试成绩。这与美国哈佛大学的一项研究结果不同，该研究得出的结论是，因天气原因偶尔缺课几天并不会损害学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The Harvard study examined seven years of school results data and could not find any impact from snow closures. What caused more disruption was when schools tried to stay open in bad weather, even though many staff and pupils were absent. But weather can make a difference to school results, according to another piece of Harvard research published last summer. It’s hot weather that has the negative impact. The results of 10 million school students were examined over 13 years and researchers found a “significant” link between years with extremely hot weather and lower results.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 哈佛大学的研究检查了七年的学校成绩数据，没有发现积雪封雪的任何影响。造成更多干扰的是，尽管许多教职员工和学生缺席，但学校仍试图在恶劣天气下保持开放。但根据哈佛大学去年夏天发表的另一项研究，天气会对学校成绩产生影响。炎热的天气会带来负面影响。对 13 年来 1000 万在校学生的成绩进行了检查，研究人员发现，天气极热的年份与成绩较低的年份之间存在“显着”联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) It’s obvious that students should go to school every day to get the most out of education. In cases of extreme weather students don’t always have that option. However, research shows that authorised absences from school such as during extreme weather are less problematic for students than absences that are not authorised. This is because unauthorised absences tend to reflect patterns and behaviours of student disengagement, or the possible negative attitudes of parents towards education that students adopt and carry with them through schooling. The level of impact on students’ educational performance is all to do with the length of time that a student is absent from school and how regularly this occurs.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 显然，学生应该每天去学校才能充分利用教育。在极端天气的情况下，学生并不总是有这种选择。然而，研究表明，在极端天气等情况下，授权缺勤对学生来说比未经授权缺勤的问题要小。这是因为未经授权的缺勤往往反映出学生脱离参与的模式和行为，或者家长对学生在学校接受和携带的教育可能持的消极态度。对学生学习成绩的影响程度与学生缺课的时间长短以及缺课的频率有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. There is opposition to the practice of giving children assignments to take home before extreme weather forces a school closure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 有人反对在极端天气迫使学校停课之前给儿童布置作业带回家的做法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. New policies adopted by many U.S. schools require students to do online learning at home in case of a school closure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 美国许多学校采取的新政策要求学生在学校停课时在家进行在线学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. According to some research, extreme hot weather negatively affects students’ performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 根据一些研究，极端炎热的天气会对学生的表现产生负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. There is a time-honoured tradition in the U.S. for school kids to stay at home on “snow days”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 在美国，学生们在“下雪天”呆在家里有一个由来已久的传统。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Debates on social media show some parents are opposed to ending the “snow day” tradition.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 社交媒体上的争论表明，一些家长反对结束“雪天”传统。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. In more northern regions of the U.S., school is less likely to be affected by snowy weather.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 在美国较北部的地区，学校不太可能受到降雪天气的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Research indicates absences from school with permission do not cause as many problems as those without permission.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 研究表明，经许可缺课不会造成与未经许可缺课那么多的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. There is objection to e-learning days owing to fear that students with no access to the Internet at home will suffer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 有人反对电子学习日，因为担心在家无法上网的学生会受到影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. In a pilot programme, students are given electronic devices to do assignments when schools are closed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 在一项试点计划中，学校停课时，为学生提供电子设备来完成作业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A long-standing debate is going on over the impact of school absences on students’ academic performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 关于缺课对学生学业成绩的影响，长期以来一直存在争论。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It may sound surprising, but you don’t have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History. I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这听起来可能令人惊讶，但你不必对时尚感兴趣，甚至不必对历史感兴趣，也能享受《着装规范：时尚法则如何创造历史》一书。我碰巧对两者都感兴趣，最终出于完全不同的原因喜欢这本书。

paragraphs.sourceText: Richard Thompson Ford is a law professor, and you probably won’t forget that for even one page. His carefully reasoned arguments, packed with examples, sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier. You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again.
paragraphs.translationZh: 理查德·汤普森·福特（Richard Thompson Ford）是一位法学教授，你可能不会忘记这一点，哪怕只是一页。他精心推理的论点，充满了例子，听起来几乎就像在阅读法庭意见，只是可能更加冗长。你可能再也不会认为时尚是一件小事了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ford’s thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. Through this lens, he shows us that the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 福特的论点是，理解特定时尚在任何特定时代意味着什么的最好方法是看看它们受到的限制。通过这个镜头，他向我们展示了 1200 年代通过的第一部法律，确保只有贵族才能穿着某些面料、颜色和装饰品，这反映了中产阶级的崛起，他们现在能够模仿其中一些时尚。上层阶级的地位受到威胁；时尚是保存它的工具。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ford takes the reader through the evolution of fashion while examining the underlying motivations of status, sex, power, and personality, which, he assumes, influenced all innovations in fashion in the past and which continue to influence us today. His writing is more than a little dense — dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. But there’s also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. No one is spared his sharp analysis: not the easy targets of 19th century women’s crippling (伤害身体的) fashions nor the modern uniforms of Silicon Valley T-shirts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 福特带领读者了解时尚的演变，同时审视地位、性别、权力和个性的潜在动机，他认为这些动机影响了过去时尚的所有创新，并继续影响着我们今天。他的写作非常密集——充满了研究、从句以及精确的形容词和名词。但也有幽默和足够有趣的情节，使写作有吸引力。没有人能幸免于他的尖锐分析：不是 19 世纪女性身体伤害时尚的容易攻击目标，也不是硅谷 T 恤的现代制服。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. Ford asks us to question unconscious beliefs, to realize that we almost never do so, to understand that the simplest choices are charged with meaning, and yet that meaning can and does change all the time. Consider the fact that a 1918 catalog insisted that boys and girls be dressed in the appropriate color. We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it’s not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但这本书（关于时尚！）的最大优势在于它的知识深度。福特要求我们质疑无意识的信念，认识到我们几乎从未这样做过，了解最简单的选择都充满意义，但这种意义可以而且确实一直在变化。考虑一下这样一个事实：1918 年的目录坚持要求男孩和女孩穿着适当的颜色。我们相信我们今天的思维已经进化了；福特向我们展示了事实并非如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. What does the author think of the book Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 作者对《着装规范：时尚法则如何创造历史》一书有何看法？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The art of persuasion means convincing others to agree with your point of view or to follow your course of action. For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说服的艺术意味着说服他人同意你的观点或遵循你的行动方针。对于我们中的一些人来说，说服是一种本能，影响力是自然而然的。对于我们其他人来说，说服技巧是可以随着时间的推移而学习和发展的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Employers place a great value on employees with persuasion skills because they can impact several aspects of job performance. Besides, teamwork and leadership rely heavily on the power of persuasion to get things done. Without persuasion skills, employees may not be as committed to or convinced of the importance of an organization’s vision and long-term mission. Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it’ll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 雇主非常重视具有说服能力的员工，因为他们可以影响工作绩效的多个方面。此外，团队合作和领导力在很大程度上依赖于说服力来完成事情。如果没有说服技巧，员工可能不会致力于或不相信组织愿景和长期使命的重要性。有效运用说服技巧不仅有助于让您的同事对您的想法感到兴奋，还可以帮助您激励他们实现共同目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: In order to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace, you need to understand how to handle conflicts and reach agreements. Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. Before you can get somebody on-board with your goal, you should help them understand why they should pursue it. Using visual aids to back up your ideas can help communicate your ideas better and make compelling arguments so your listeners will come to a logical choice and become fully committed to your ideas and plans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了在工作场所学习说服的艺术，您需要了解如何处理冲突并达成协议。良好的沟通是有效说服的第一步，但逻辑和推理也同样重要。在让某人实现你的目标之前，你应该帮助他们理解为什么他们应该追求这个目标。使用视觉辅助工具来支持您的想法可以帮助更好地传达您的想法并提出令人信服的论据，以便您的听众做出合乎逻辑的选择并完全致力于您的想法和计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: Successful persuasion skills are based on your ability to have positive interactions and maintain meaningful relationships with people. In order to sustain those relationships, you must be able to work in their best interests as well. Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. The more they achieve and the greater progress they make, the more they trust your judgement and strength.
paragraphs.translationZh: 成功的说服技巧取决于您与人进行积极互动并维持有意义的关系的能力。为了维持这些关系，您也必须能够为他们的最大利益着想。当你的同事与你一起取得成功时，他们更有可能同意你的观点。他们取得的成就越多、进步越大，他们就越相信你的判断和力量。

paragraphs.sourceText: We persuade and get persuaded every day — we’re either convincing or being convinced. A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们每天都在说服和被说服——我们要么被说服，要么被说服。与传统的组织结构相比，绝大多数人更喜欢协作和团队合作；没有人喜欢被告知要做什么或被摆布。因此，组织和领导者应该采用强大的说服技巧来带来必要的改变。
